title: Memory vs latency tinkerpad — quant + caching notes
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad to collect intuition, micro-experiments, and follow-ups about memory / latency tradeoffs for long-context serving when using low-bit quantization and cache strategies. Not polished. Notes to self and tiny TODOs mixed in.

High-level intuition notes:
- KV cache hits reduce work roughly proportional to skipped autoregressive tokens, but overhead per request is non-zero (lookup, copy into GPU memory, potential re-compaction). For 1–2k prefix hits this is big win; for many small hits (hundreds of clients each with tiny caches) overhead can dominate.
- Quantization (4-bit/2-bit) reduces memory pressure enabling larger batch/KV capacity but adds per-token kernel overhead depending on dequant strategy. The sweet spot depends on sequence-length distribution and request concurrency.
- Memory fragmentation on multi-model hosts (mixed precisions) makes tail-latency worse than mean-latency improvements suggest. Need to measure p95/p99 with realistic mix.

Quick lit & links I want to re-read:
- FlashAttention/flash-attn optimizations (check notes on fusion + kernel launch overhead) — re-evaluate with Q4 quant kernels.
- QLoRA/LoRA + 4-bit post-training quant papers — good for fine-tuned LMs where accuracy must be preserved.
- Papers/threads on product of experts / KV-MoE for cache routing (idea: route cache reads to small per-client adapters).

Micro-experiments to run (short names + accept/abort criteria):
1) baseline-host: baseline fp16 model, no KV cache, perf profiles for seq=512,1024,2048 at 4 concurrency levels.
   - Accept if p95 latency < target (60ms token gen) at target throughput.
2) 4-bit-static: convert weights to 4-bit per-channel, use dequant-on-the-fly kernels (naive). Measure throughput and memory.
   - Abort if top-1 quality drop > 2% on eval prompts (use our eval harness).
3) cache-enabled-small: enable prefix KV cache for conversational prefix reuse patterns, measure p50/p95 improvement and extra overhead (copy time).
4) hybrid-quant-cache: combine 4-bit + KV cache, run tail-latency stress test with 500 small sessions. Check for memory fragmentation and OOM events.

Observations to capture when running experiments:
- timeline: kernel init times, buffer allocation peaks (heap snapshots), copy-to-device durations for every request, dequant times per layer.
- perf counters: GPU util, SM occupancy, kernel launch counts, PCIe copy times (when not colocated).

Rough code/ops checklist (things I keep forgetting):
- ensure allocator uses pooled allocator with maximum headroom set (avoid sudden growth spikes).
- pin small KV cache pages into contiguous region to reduce fragmentation (experimentally test cudaMallocManaged vs cudaMalloc).
- add metrics: cache_hit_size_histogram (not just hit rate), dequant_time_ms, kv_copy_bytes_per_request.

Open questions / hypothesis:
- H1: For medium-length contexts (1k–3k) and >8 concurrent streams, 4-bit quantization + cache wins both cost and latency vs fp16 without cache. Need to confirm with p99 metrics.
- H2: For many tiny sessions (<=128 tokens), cost of cache bookkeeping + dequant dominates; opportunistic batching at ingress may be better.
- Q: can we route small sessions to a CPU-backed model variant with tiny memory to keep GPU for bulk jobs? Cost tradeoffs unclear.

Short-term action items (who/when):
- Leah: set up baseline-host experiments (GH-PR: perf-runner changes) — target 2027-11-05.
- Omar: prototype dequant kernel profiling hooks and add dequant_time_ms metric — target 2027-11-08.
- Mika: sketch allocator experiment (pinned vs pooled) and run memory fragmentation microbench — target 2027-11-10.

Notes to self: stick to incremental changes; isolate variables. When measuring p99, run >= 10k requests per config with realistic inter-arrival distributions (not uniform).

Fragments / rough scratch ideas I might flesh later:
- "micro-shard" approach: put popular prefixes into a tiny read-only model shard in higher-precision to avoid dequant for hot cache reads. Could reduce tail latency if hot set small.
- heuristic: if client session length < 256 and request rate < 1req/min, serve from on-demand small instance (cheaper) rather than keeping KV cache. Build policy in routing plane.

References / quick bookmarks I keep returning to:
- internal: CONFLUENCE: KV cache design (linked above)
- GH: PR 4521 (serving-runtime: add per-layer dequant hook)
- external: blog posts on quantization tradeoffs (fast.ai threads, source refs noted in team slack)

End-of-file quick TODO: convert selected results into a short one-pager for eng-ops (p95 focus) and put any non-provisional code behind feature flag.

-- Leah (notes saved 2027-11-02)
